name: Frontend UI design
blurb: Distinctive, accessible web UI: design direction, tokens, states, motion, WCAG 2.2, break testing, audits and redesigns.
searches: anti AI slop frontend design skill Claude new
agent skill UI review accessibility WCAG 2.2
shadcn Tailwind v4 design system agent skill
web animation easing springs skill design engineering
DESIGN.md design system file for coding agents

tests.prompt: Build a landing page for a small Edinburgh bakery that takes pickup orders online. No brand assets yet; they bake sourdough and pastries from 5 am.
tests.good: States a Design Read and mode (Persuade) first; explores the bakery's domain and colour world; names and avoids defaults (centred gradient hero, 3 feature cards, cream+terracotta serif); token block with one accent; real specific copy, no invented reviews or stats; working order CTA with all button states; image slots or real images, no div-drawn mockups; reduced-motion fallback; checked at 320 px and desktop.

tests.prompt: Review this React team-members list component for UI problems before I ship it. [component with avatar, name, email, role badge, member count and a ••• menu]
tests.good: Builds worst-case data (long unbroken email, one-letter name, missing role, count of 1, 1,000 rows, RTL), lists breaks with severity and a concrete CSS/code fix each (min-width:0, flex-shrink:0, overflow-wrap:anywhere, Intl.PluralRules, tabular-nums, virtualisation), checks keyboard access and focus on the menu, uses a Before/After/Why table, and asks before applying design decisions.

tests.prompt: Add animation to our dropdown menu, command palette (Cmd+K) and toast notifications.
tests.good: Refuses or minimises animation on the command palette (keyboard, used constantly); dropdown scales from ~0.96 with origin at the trigger, 150-200 ms ease-out with a named cubic-bezier token; toasts use transitions so rapid toasts retarget and exit the way they entered; only transform/opacity; never scale(0); prefers-reduced-motion fallback; no bounce.

tests.prompt: Redesign the settings page of our Next.js + Tailwind v4 app so it stops looking generic. Our Figma library holds the colour and spacing variables and the code has drifted from them. Also add an end-to-end test for the new save flow.
tests.good: States a short plan first: redesign here (redesign.md, visual-system.md, components-and-states.md), tokens through figma-design (design-tokens.md and token-sync-and-drift.md: export the Figma variables and map them, never invent new values), the test through testing-qa (playwright-e2e.md: role-based locators, web-first assertions, no fixed waits). Reports what it will keep before changing anything; builds every state of the save flow (saving, saved, error, disabled); checks the Done means of all three crafts and says what wasn't verified.

tests.prompt: Our admin app is Next.js (App Router) with MUI v7. It looks like every other Material app. Restyle it to our brand (one teal accent, our type scale and an 8 px radius), add a light/dark toggle that doesn't flash on first load, and rebuild the Users table page with proper loading, empty and error states. It must meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
tests.good: Brand lives in one `createTheme` with `cssVariables: true` and `colorSchemes: { light, dark }` (palette, typography scale, `shape.borderRadius: 8`, spacing), component changes in `theme.components.Mui*.styleOverrides`/`variants`, not scattered `sx` literals or global `.Mui*` CSS overrides; Next.js wiring is right: `AppRouterCacheProvider` from `@mui/material-nextjs` in the root layout, `InitColorSchemeScript` to stop the flash, the toggle through `useColorScheme` (handling `mode` being undefined before mount), dark styles via `theme.applyStyles('dark', …)` rather than `palette.mode` ternaries; the stock Material tells are removed on purpose (Roboto, uppercase buttons via `textTransform: 'none'`, default blue, elevation shadows on every surface) while keeping one accent; the table has skeleton rows while loading, an empty state with the next action, an error with retry, long names truncated with the full value available, and works at 320 px (DataGrid only if `@mui/x-data-grid` is already installed); accessibility checked in both schemes: custom palette at 4.5:1 text and 3:1 UI, visible focus rings not overridden away, icon buttons with `aria-label`, table headers and caption; v7 APIs only (Grid `size` prop, no `makeStyles`/`@mui/styles`), no uninstalled packages, current docs checked through the MUI MCP (`npx -y @mui/mcp@latest`) or llms.txt when available, and says what was not rendered or verified.

tools.name: Tailwind CSS
tools.why: Most used CSS framework in the State of CSS 2025 survey (about 37% of respondents), with the most happy and retained users.

tools.name: shadcn/ui
tools.why: Most popular Tailwind component library in 2026 round-ups and the repo has 125k GitHub stars; it ships an official agent skill and MCP server.

tools.name: Figma
tools.why: Default design tool in UI design workflows (Figma kits for shadcn/Tailwind each have hundreds of thousands of community users) and it publishes an official MCP server and skills for design-to-code.

tools.name: Storybook
tools.why: The standard tool for building, documenting and testing UI components in isolation (91k GitHub stars), now with an official MCP server and a11y addon.

tools.name: Base UI / Radix UI
tools.why: Radix Primitives is what shadcn/ui is built on and Base UI (stable, v1.x) is the maintained successor option in shadcn presets, so they are the default accessible primitives for React.

tools.name: Motion (Framer Motion)
tools.why: The leading React animation library (33k GitHub stars; `framer-motion` is now an alias of `motion`) and its author ships an official AI kit with skill and MCP.

tools.name: axe-core
tools.why: The engine behind Storybook's a11y addon, Lighthouse and Playwright a11y tests (wcag22aa tag, 7.6k stars); Deque cites it catching up to 57% of WCAG issues automatically.

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP / Lighthouse
tools.why: Official Google MCP (53k stars) lets agents inspect, screenshot, profile and run Lighthouse in a real browser; Lighthouse is the standard a11y/performance audit (31k stars).

tools.name: Playwright
tools.why: Common way to run axe, screenshots at several widths and keyboard flows against the rendered UI; official MCP has 38k stars. Test authoring itself belongs to testing-qa.

tools.name: v0
tools.why: Vercel's AI UI generator outputting React, Tailwind and shadcn/ui, named in 2026 UI-generation round-ups; has a Platform API and TypeScript SDK.

tools.name: Google Stitch
tools.why: Google's AI UI design tool with an official MCP and a skills repo (8.4k stars) that exports DESIGN.md design systems; named in the craft's DESIGN.md guide.

tools.name: React Aria
tools.why: Adobe's accessible hooks and components (16k stars) named as the top-tier primitive option for complex widgets like comboboxes and date pickers; publishes llms.txt docs.

tools.name: MUI (Material UI)
tools.why: Most used React UI library in the State of React 2025 survey (57.2% of respondents, just ahead of shadcn/ui) with 95k GitHub stars and about 4M weekly npm downloads; ships an official MCP server (@mui/mcp) and llms.txt docs. The guides never name it.

tools.name: Bootstrap
tools.why: Second most used CSS framework in State of CSS 2025 (1,194 respondents vs Tailwind's 2,041) and by far the most deployed on the web: W3Techs (Sept 2026) puts it on 13.4% of all sites and 74.8% of sites that use a CSS framework. Redesigns of existing sites meet it constantly; the guides never name it.

tools.name: Sass / SCSS
tools.why: The most used styling tool after plain CSS: 2,434 State of CSS 2025 respondents use Sass/SCSS, more than use Tailwind (2,041) and well ahead of PostCSS (1,517). Bootstrap and many existing design systems are themed through it; Dart Sass is the only maintained implementation and @import is deprecated in favour of @use/@forward. The guides never name it.

tools.name: Ant Design
tools.why: Third most used React UI library in State of React 2025 and the usual choice for enterprise dashboards and admin panels (93k GitHub stars, about 1.5M weekly npm downloads); v6 docs ship an MCP server, llms.txt, a design.md and a token-based theme API.

tools.name: Lucide
tools.why: Open-source icon set of 1,600+ SVG icons with packages for React, Vue, Svelte, Angular and more; the default icon library in shadcn/ui projects, so it is the icon family most AI-built React UIs already use.
